{"title":"Support imported 3D meshes as Eidolons","status":"done","priority":"medium","created":"2026-10-04","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["eidolons","3d-rendering","assets"],"description":"## Goal
Allow an Eidolon recipe to depict an entity with an imported 3D mesh while preserving Quod's Prolog-owned rendering vocabulary, subject identity, authorization and existing mark reconciliation.

## Delivery
1. Add a typed mesh-asset geometry to the existing `part/6 → model/2 → mark/7` path. Define portable embedded-material semantics (`asset_surfaces`), integer-mm placement, asset-local bounds/pivot/front, occurrence scale and labels at the shared schema/decoder seam.
2. Render a validated, self-contained static GLB profile through the current Babylon client. Pin the loader; reject unsupported features, external dependencies and unlisted extensions before loading. Verify digest and actual resource use under Prolog-authorized budgets. Test embedded textures with production CSP in a browser.
3. Extend the scene-owned resource service for verified model bytes and a shared decoded template with per-occurrence instances. Two placements must retain distinct transforms and picking identities. Unchanged or transform-only refreshes must not refetch/redecode; removal, replacement and late async completion must release resources safely.
4. Add a pinned offline import/validation workflow for FBX and common source formats (GLB/glTF, OBJ, STL, polygon PLY) into the defined GLB profile. Record source/output digests, importer/version/options, diagnostics and provenance. Verify fidelity with real FBX fixtures before claiming support.

## Acceptance and architectural boundary
- Exercise the Prolog validator and real cross-ontology subject/access policy, plus an asymmetric model with off-centre pivot, rotated parent, multiple submeshes/materials and two occurrences.
- Test rejection of bad digest/profile, missing external resources, unsupported glTF features and exceeded actual resource allowances. Resource budgets are ontology policy, not hidden Erlang/JS constants.
- Keep imported node names/extras from creating subjects or permissions. Public packaged assets may be the first slice; private delivery requires a separate authorization path.
- Static GLB does not require a new scene graph process or NIF. Record stable visual/physical identity, transform composition and collider separation for later shared scene/physics work. A live native physics query cannot be used inside a proof that seals a durable diff; later observations require authenticated producer binding and ordinary authorized actions/transactions.

{"title":"Add shared-world physics simulation and authenticated consequences","status":"in-progress","priority":"medium","created":"2026-10-04","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["physics","world","native-runtime"],"description":"## Goal
Add authoritative, recoverable physics simulation for a shared world while keeping domain state, policy, actions, authorization and meaningful consequences in Prolog. Treat native physics as transient world state, not a second domain engine.

## Delivery
1. Define world-local physical bodies, colliders, joints/attachments, authority, epoch, incarnation and structural revision in ontology-owned state. Visual Eidolons and physical shapes are separate; a GLB's triangles or declared visual bounds do not silently become collision authority.
2. Install one retained simulation owner for each active simulated world through the existing runtime/resource lifecycle. It consumes committed desired state, steps Rapier through audited Rustler NIF calls, and publishes current epoch/tick body poses. Physics is optional and enabled by committed Prolog policy, not inferred from whether a scene looks static; a nonphysical world starts no simulator. Respect bounded native work, BEAM scheduler safety, reader/writer locking and native failure retirement; reuse existing owners and notifications.
3. Compose parent/local scene transforms with body motion under a single pose source per occurrence. Bind frames to stable entity/body identity plus authority epoch, simulation incarnation, structural revision and tick. Reconnect and sequence gaps rebuild from current state; stale frames and deleted/recreated entities cannot resurrect or move an object.
4. Filter motion frames and perception candidates through each agent's current authorized view. Keep visual/perception bounds separate from collision bounds. Measure whether existing Rapier/Parry queries suffice before adding another spatial index; any index is a derived projection of the world owner, never a second knowledge base.
5. Admit bounded, quantized contact/obstruction observations from an authenticated physics producer through the existing reaction/action/atomic transaction path. Prolog decides their meaning and durable effects. Current sealing rejects a write proof that reads a live native query; do not add a functor exemption or classify live physics as proof-bound. Bind observations to world/authority incarnation, entity/body revision and tick, reject stale/duplicate reports, and preserve owner recovery without replaying old reactions.

## Acceptance
- A chair can be pushed without a label/material refresh snapping it back; a structural edit or authority restart invalidates old frames.
- A hinged door can be obstructed: physics reports the observation, Prolog decides and atomically commits the domain consequence. An in-proof live physics query is rejected.
- A held object follows its holder and survives attach/drop, deletion, reconnect and current-authority recovery according to an explicit checkpoint policy.
- Unauthorized viewers receive neither hidden scene objects nor their motion frames. Collider-less or visually larger objects are not lost from perception selection.
- Native stepping and queries do not block an ontology state owner or ordinary BEAM schedulers; failures retire the affected world visibly. Repeated unchanged checks do not rebuild Prolog/history state or cause disk writes; real updates still apply.

This is separate from static GLB mesh rendering, which can be delivered first without a physics NIF. Direction and caveats: [world overview](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/world.md), [archived client/world direction](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/outdated/client-world-direction.md), [archived consequence direction](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/outdated/world-consequence-direction.md), and [current multiwrite map](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/multiwrite-architecture.md). The archived consequence draft's in-proof `physics_contact/2` path conflicts with current sealing and is not an implementation recipe.

## Delivery boundaries after the ontology/space review
Completed foundations remain [QUD.4](nimbalyst://QUD.4)–[QUD.8](nimbalyst://QUD.8). Remaining normal-world integration is [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27), with governed space vocabulary in [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33); actual-lobby player/Vive acceptance is [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26) and deferred real-lobby blocked/closed door acceptance is [QUD.36](nimbalyst://QUD.36). Keep this umbrella open alongside the existing held-object, authorized query, distinct-impact and multi-viewer tasks.

Ontology and space are independent classes. Reuse the existing subscribed committed-diff path for live collider definitions; do not impose recipe re-adoption or duplicate synchronization on every live edit. No backward-compatibility requirement or parallel old/new engine is introduced. Same lobby identity/history preservation and applicable validator/deployment authority still apply. Text/3D ontology editing is separate work, not a blanket prerequisite for this physics umbrella.","activity":[{"id":"activity_1791119703505_n87t","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"action":"created","timestamp":1791119703505},{"id":"activity_1791119719370_nn2f","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"action":"updated","field":"description","oldValue":"## Goal

"Build a Quod-owned Rapier/Rustler integration with pinned dependencies, build/release/CI support and an adapter independent of ontology semantics. Use the existing world/runtime ownership path to install an active-world simulator as a sole mutating caller; define exactly what happens across snapshot replacement, queue backpressure, replay, authority transfer and native failure. Audit step/query cost, dirty CPU scheduling or bounded yielding, memory ownership, bounded pose/contact output and idle-world behavior. Do not copy bbsvx's ordinary locked NIF calls unchanged. Test through the real owner that unchanged installation does not rebuild history or write/sync files, changed physical definitions apply, a sleeping world need not step/publish, and recoverable native failures retire the selected world visibly without a poison-definition retry loop. A native abort cannot be contained by an in-process NIF; apply the recorded port fallback decision if audit shows that risk unacceptable. Reference: /home/yan/src/quod/doc/outdated/client-world-direction.md §8.

## Current contract and first delivery
Use [the current world contract](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/world.md) as the authority for semantics; the archived engine notes are background. Physics is optional: a space with simulation disabled starts neither the physics agent nor the native resource. For the first profile, run one simulator on the node selected by the hosted physics agent's committed assignment. Other nodes may view the result; different spaces may use different hosts. Sharing one space's body calculations among hosts is out of scope.

First deliver a server-side fixture with a ground collider and one falling body, installed through the real resource owner. Demonstrate optional startup, finite stepping/querying, retained state on unchanged reconciliation, changed-body installation, policy-owned resource allowances, and clean resource retirement. Keep native calculations separate from Prolog domain decisions. Then exercise same-host generation changes, host replacement, replay/collapse retirement, and stale frame/sample rejection. Resolve uncertain activation through original request/outcome custody; do not adopt a generation belonging to a dead incarnation or treat timeout as rejection. This activation/recovery requirement belongs to the foundation and must not be deferred to the later durable-impact task.

Deliver the adapter, production resource integration, meaningful owner/lifecycle tests, native safety audit, and measured step/query/scheduler costs with retained logs. The door task then proves the first semantic interaction. Client motion, user controls, general agent queries and durable impact consequences are separate follow-on slices."

Do not copy Prolog state into a second view KB."

{"title":"Synchronize Nimbalyst tracker items to Forgejo issues","status":"done","priority":"high","created":"2026-10-04","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["forgejo","tracker","integration"],"description":"## Goal

## Work
1. Confirm the target Forgejo repository, deployed version, API capabilities, credentials and item visibility. Identify an integration point in Nimbalyst that emits durable create/update/archive/delete events; its currently exposed GitHub importer is inbound and is not this outbound sync.
2. Define the item mapping: stable Nimbalyst item ID to Forgejo repository/issue index, title/body, type, status, priority, tags/labels, assignee where representable, dependencies and canonical Nimbalyst link. Define how Nimbalyst-local IDs become stable shared IDs before a collaborative rollout.
3. On Nimbalyst create/update/status change, create or update exactly one mapped Forgejo issue. On Nimbalyst delete, propagate the deletion to the mapped issue using the deployed Forgejo's supported mechanism. Explicitly define whether this is hard deletion or closure/archival, how comments/history are handled, and how a tombstone prevents accidental recreation. Resolve that policy with Yan before enabling destructive propagation.
4. Make delivery resilient: persist mapping and last applied version, process events in order per item, retry transient failures without duplicates, reconcile after outages, and expose pending/failed state. Restrict Forgejo credentials to issue operations and redact them from logs.
5. Bootstrap existing Nimbalyst tracker items, including the Eidolon and physics tasks, without duplicate Forgejo issues. Preserve dependency links where Forgejo supports them; otherwise link to canonical Nimbalyst items. Verify every created issue's full body because current local tracker collaborative-body writes have failed.
6. Test create, edit, close/reopen, delete, repeated delivery, outage recovery and manual Forgejo-side drift against real tracker and Forgejo API seams. Document the one-way authority and how to repair a failed sync.

## Acceptance
A Nimbalyst item is automatically created, edited and removed/closed in Forgejo according to the agreed deletion policy, with no duplicate issue or feedback loop. Initial items reconcile once, mappings survive restart, failures are visible and retryable, and the Nimbalyst tracker remains the only authoritative issue state.

1. Confirm the target Forgejo repository, deployed version, API capabilities, credentials and item visibility. Identify an integration point in Nimbalyst that emits durable create/update/archive/delete events; its currently exposed GitHub importer is inbound and is not this outbound sync.
2. Define the item mapping: stable Nimbalyst item ID to Forgejo repository/issue index, title/body, type, status, priority, tags/labels, assignee where representable, dependencies and canonical Nimbalyst link. Define how Nimbalyst-local IDs become stable shared IDs before a collaborative rollout.
3. On Nimbalyst create/update/status change, create or update exactly one mapped Forgejo issue. On Nimbalyst delete, propagate the deletion to the mapped issue using the deployed Forgejo's supported mechanism. Explicitly define whether this is hard deletion or closure/archival, how comments/history are handled, and how a tombstone prevents accidental recreation. Resolve that policy with Yan before enabling destructive propagation.
4. Make delivery resilient: persist mapping and last applied version, process events in order per item, retry transient failures without duplicates, reconcile after outages, and expose pending/failed state. Restrict Forgejo credentials to issue operations and redact them from logs.
5. Bootstrap existing Nimbalyst tracker items, including the Eidolon and physics tasks, without duplicate Forgejo issues. Preserve dependency links where Forgejo supports them; otherwise link to canonical Nimbalyst items. Verify every created issue's full body because current local tracker collaborative-body writes have failed.
6. Test create, edit, close/reopen, delete, repeated delivery, outage recovery and manual Forgejo-side drift against real tracker and Forgejo API seams. Document the one-way authority and how to repair a failed sync.

## Acceptance
A Nimbalyst item is automatically created, edited and removed/closed in Forgejo according to the agreed deletion policy, with no duplicate issue or feedback loop. Initial items reconcile once, mappings survive restart, failures are visible and retryable, and the Nimbalyst tracker remains the only authoritative issue state.

This is an integration task spanning Nimbalyst and Forgejo; it is not a Quod Prolog/runtime feature."

Reuse the authenticated sample/action path established by the door task and the checkpoint machinery from the chair task. This adds occurrence semantics, not a second observation or transaction engine.

Give each occurrence an immutable identity/payload under the current run. In one existing atomic transaction establish acceptance/deduplication state, domain and receiver consequences, and compatible recovery checkpoints at or after the event. Equal payloads from distinct impacts remain distinct; repeated delivery cannot repeat a consequence. Maintain explicit bounded unsent retention, loss accounting and restart discontinuities under Prolog policy.

Before enabling non-idempotent consequences, prove that the original operation reference, exact signed request and outcome binding remain resolvable after worker timeout and loss of the host's local state. Trace existing transaction custody/recovery and extend its existing owner only for a demonstrated missing capability. Do not assume the hosted actor's volatile queue supplies durability, add an outbox, resubmit an uncertain action, or advance past it merely because its deadline expired. The current contract blocks later durable occurrences while an earlier outcome remains uncertain; any alternative needs a separately verified contract change, including prepared atomic transactions.

Acceptance: two equal impacts apply separately; duplicates do not; old-run and old-revision samples fail; a lost reply is resolved without new submission; crashes before submission, after durable admission, after commit and before result delivery have explicit outcomes. Restore interacting checkpoint groups without turning overlap correction into impacts or rewinding accepted consequences. Verify multi-ontology all-or-nothing effects, queue saturation, explicit loss, and no replayed historical reactions through production seams. "Implement distinct impact occurrences with durable domain consequences according to [the world contract](/home/yan/src/quod/doc/world.md) and [repository rules](/home/yan/src/quod/AGENTS.md). Reuse the authenticated sample/action path established by the door task and the checkpoint machinery from the chair task. This adds occurrence semantics, not a second observation or transaction engine.

Give each occurrence an immutable identity/payload under the current run. In one existing atomic transaction establish acceptance/deduplication state, domain and receiver consequences, and compatible recovery checkpoints at or after the event. Equal payloads from distinct impacts remain distinct; repeated delivery cannot repeat a consequence. Maintain explicit bounded unsent retention, loss accounting and restart discontinuities under Prolog policy.

Before enabling non-idempotent consequences, prove that the original operation reference, exact signed request and outcome binding remain resolvable after worker timeout and loss of the host's local state. Trace existing transaction custody/recovery and extend its existing owner only for a demonstrated missing capability. Do not assume the hosted actor's volatile queue supplies durability, add an outbox, resubmit an uncertain action, or advance past it merely because its deadline expired. The current contract blocks later durable occurrences while an earlier outcome remains uncertain; any alternative needs a separately verified contract change, including prepared atomic transactions.

Acceptance: two equal impacts apply separately; duplicates do not; old-run and old-revision samples fail; a lost reply is resolved without new submission; crashes before submission, after durable admission, after commit and before result delivery have explicit outcomes. Restore interacting checkpoint groups without turning overlap correction into impacts or rewinding accepted consequences. Verify multi-ontology all-or-nothing effects, queue saturation, explicit loss, and no replayed historical reactions through production seams. Report actual parser/resource limits; do not split a single atomic consequence to evade them. Scope exclusions: motion rendering, distributed simulation within a space, and lossless capture before durable submission."

3. Render the door and obstacle through existing Eidolon/mark composition. Bind stable anchored subjects and body identities to their visual occurrences; a mark ID, recipe or mesh digest is not physical identity.

5. Expose the close action and the minimum authorized obstacle-edit/reset controls through the existing ontology-authored GUI/action paths. Show committed closing, blocked and closed state, and truthful pending/unavailable or recovery status. Native braking or an elapsed animation alone must not claim a durable outcome.
6. Preserve proof-console use and playing/edition recipes. Match the supplied picture's agreed visual requirements without broadening into a general world editor.

Invariants
Domain state, permissions, budgets and consequences remain in Prolog. Use the retained simulator, hosted actor, reaction matcher and existing atomic transaction owners. Preserve exact-operation custody/resolution, revision and incarnation fencing, and atomic consequence/checkpoint commits. Unknown originals require exact resolution or authorized cancellation, never inferred rejection or resubmission. Restore current state without replaying reactions. Keep one pose source per body-driven occurrence; appearance refresh must not reset it. No scripted obstruction substitute, live native predicate in durable proofs, sealing exemption, polling loop, broker or private state engine.

Acceptance
- In a real client view, authorized close visibly moves the door. With an obstacle it stops and displays the committed blocked outcome; with the obstruction cleared it closes and displays the committed closed outcome.
- Competing edits, duplicate/delayed observations, stale frames, deletion/recreation, refresh, simulator restart and reconnect cannot act on or move the wrong object.
- Required observation delivery survives queue pressure; uncertainty remains visible with an authorized resolution/cancellation path.
- Committed stopped geometry restores without replaying completion reactions. Unchanged reconciliation retains the simulator and resources without replaying history, rebuilding or writing/syncing state.
- Verify through real production seams and browser interaction, including the preserved console flow and visual comparison to the attached reference. Run applicable client/native/server gates sequentially, retaining full logs, failures and true exits.
- Finish with a concrete account of what works, how it was verified, the actual production delta and remaining limitations.

Workflow and boundaries
Proceed autonomously through the selected implementation and verification; follow AGENTS.md. Do not initiate Claude consultation. This task does not authorize deployment, data migration, state wiping, hot client controls, remote multi-viewer expansion or unrelated lobby-device work. {"title":"Bind nested call-chain members to the parent scope's sealed transcript","status":"to-do","priority":"medium","created":"2026-10-06","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["prolog","acl","consensus","engine"],"description":"Follow-up from the system-ontology ACL review (local item QUD.20, task_1791240698839_ywd2cg), question Q1 of the Fable review on 2026-10-06.

## Context

`can_invoke/4` receives the inter-ontology call chain as a list of namespace names (src/predicates/quod_ask.erl, `chain_identities`). The head of a recorded chain is bound to the target and the tail to the proof origin at commit (`authorization_chain`), and the top-level entry is bound to the signed request (`quod_client_goal:authorization_transcript`). Intermediate members are written by the node executing the parent scope and are validated for shape only (`quod_scope_session:valid_invocation_input`, `quod_dtx:valid_chain`). A read-only parent reaches a child's validators only as an opaque plan digest inside an f+1 read certificate that carries no facts (`quod_read_certificate`).

## Current state

The shipped ACL implementation does NOT depend on intermediate chain members. System targets admit two exact wrapper goals and each wrapper asks root to check the authenticated principal before reading private source or opening a transaction (priv/ontologies/common_predicates.pl `system_source_administrator/0`). The only policies that still read chain shape are the pre-existing "direct request" rules: `root_direct_context/3` in quod_root.pl and `node_hosting_context/3` in node_execution.pl. This ticket is therefore hardening, not a blocker for the ACL work.

## Goal

Make an intermediate chain member verifiable, so a policy may trust "this call came through ontology X" against certified evidence rather than against the executing node's word.

## Expected change

1. Record outgoing invocations in the parent scope (child identity, goal digest, chain) in `quod_proof_session`, not only the incoming ones.
2. Carry that record in the sealed plan material (`quod_dtx:seal_material`, `encode_material`). Plan and ledger format break; no backward compatibility is required, but a re-found and data wipe follows.
3. Make the parent record available to the child's validators: through the coordinator for the atomic lane, and through the read certificate for a read-only parent (`quod_read_certificate`, `quod_dtx_coordinator`).
4. Verify at commit that each recorded chain entry with intermediate members is matched by the parent's certified outgoing record (`quod_ask:validate_authorization_entries`, `quod_commit_validation`).

## Risk and cost estimate (from reading, not measured)

- No change to the Simplex protocol itself (rounds, votes, finality, committee). The change is in what validators verify before voting.
- Moderate engineering risk: a defect in the new commit check rejects or splits commits. Week-scale engine work across 5 to 6 modules plus CT coverage.
- Performance: a few hundred bytes more per nested writable hop and one extra digest or signature check at commit. The existing per-entry `can_invoke` re-proof dominates. No extra network round trips if the record travels with the plan or certificate.

## Acceptance

- A multi-node CT case where a validator receives a chain whose intermediate member has no matching certified parent record rejects the commit, and the honest path still commits.
- Existing ask, atomic, independent and read-certificate suites stay green; the format break is documented and the re-found procedure recorded.
- `root_direct_context/3` and `node_hosting_context/3` either keep working unchanged or are updated to the new evidence explicitly, with a stated decision.

## Non-goals

No change to the Prolog ACL policies shipped under QUD.20. Yan agrees with automatic enrollment as the durable solution; manual provisioning of the current fleet alone is insufficient. No implementation has been performed for this follow-up.

Objective
Every new persistent Quod node identity automatically obtains one dedicated ordinary ontology containing its instance of the node class. Subsequent starts recover that exact identity. Define and implement consistent authority for advertising system and ordinary ontologies without making enrollment depend on root consensus membership.

Terminology and ownership
- Physical Quod runtime: loads its key, initiates enrollment and recovers its retained exact reference.
- Node identity ontology: durable node instance, active key binding, explicit ACL and ordinary hosting intentions. This is an ordinary ontology with the existing runtime, not an additional autonomous management agent/service.
- quod:node: shared node vocabulary and proposed owner of enrollment policy.
- quod:root: existing create_ontology/3 action and exact delegation to enrollment policy; system catalogue and root committee remain separately governed.
- Directory: derived leased routes; target ontology: its own ACL and membership.
Do not centralize per-node hosting configuration in root.

Observed starting point (prior deployment evidence; recheck before changing live state)
Founder has a bound node identity ontology; nine non-founder allocations lack one. Shared system ontologies are locally running. Non-founders log advertisement_author_unavailable. Creation attempted as a bare non-admitted node principal was denied.
Publisher currently partitions bootstrap/system rows from ordinary rows. System rows require a root-control author, ordinary rows a node principal. Missing authority in either nonempty partition rejects the entire publication. Merely provisioning node identities is insufficient.

Proposed enrollment
1. Reuse the restricted, key-bound enrollment pattern already present in quod:signup and root's ontology_creation_policy/2 delegation.
2. Node startup initiates the ordinary signed request once prerequisites are ready. Prolog policy derives and validates the full node founding recipe, exact requester key and identity allocation.
3. Use existing create_ontology/3, actions, atomic transactions, effect journal and lifecycle machinery. Prove how creation execution, placement on the enrolling node, self-hosting and local verified binding compose; do not assume root-side creation executes on the new node.
4. Enrollment only grants creation of the applicant's own node identity under the approved recipe. It grants neither arbitrary ontology creation nor root committee membership.
5. Retain and verify namespace, genesis anchor and node instance through the existing local pointer. Preserve one identity across process restarts and address/allocation changes.
6. Recover the original operation after uncertain outcomes or a crash between creation and binding. Never blindly reissue creation, invent replacement identity after corruption, or hide data loss.
7. Network/policy readiness uses existing notifications and recovery owners, preserving caller deadlines. No polling or second workflow engine.

Proposed advertisement policy
- A verified node identity can advertise an eligible locally ready copy.
- Shared system rows derive exact namespace/anchor authority from root's system catalogue; actor-authored system publication must not require membership in root consensus.
- Ordinary rows require exact committed hosts_ontology(NodeRef, Namespace, Anchor, discoverable).
- Private hosting rows are excluded from public generations and enumeration.
- Retain a narrow root-control bootstrap route before node identities are available, and specify publication/withdrawal when enrollment completes.
- Receiver validation verifies the active author key and appropriate committed authority for each descriptor. Reuse existing certified projections and route owner.
- Advertising does not confer target ownership, mutation access or committee membership. Target role and ACL checks remain mandatory at use.
- Amend current sender/receiver rules coherently. Do not merely suppress all system rows on non-control nodes, promote every node to root consensus, or accept arbitrary claims because a signature is valid.

Resolve in the design before implementation
- Open node enrollment versus an explicit enrollment credential/admission policy; startup automation does not by itself decide who may enroll. All limits and costs belong in Prolog.
- Uniqueness/recovery identity allocation, pending operation custody, creation executor and placement/binding sequence.
- Exact root advertisement rules after bootstrap; system membership revocation and catalogue withdrawal.
- Current discoverable hosting is the host's publication choice, not proof of target-owner publication consent. Document this boundary; stronger global confidentiality needs explicit policy.
- Root administrator invocation rights and create action prerequisites are distinct; verify actual grants instead of assuming one implies the other.
- Reconcile archived design language with current implementation and compact contracts.

Acceptance
- Real production signed paths: founder bootstrap, fresh joining node and existing fleet node without an identity enroll automatically under the selected policy.
- Restart and endpoint changes retain the same exact identity; unchanged restart performs no new creation.
- Crash before/after commit and before/after binding, duplicate request, lost response and temporary unavailability resolve the same operation without duplicate ontologies or automatic uncertain-write resubmission.
- Wrong key/anchor/instance, malformed pointer and unauthorized founding options fail closed without privilege escalation.
- Enrolled non-root-control nodes publish valid system routes and eligible ordinary routes. Invalid catalogue anchors, absent hosting facts, inactive keys and private rows are rejected/excluded.
- Removal/revocation, lease expiry and transitions between bootstrap and enrolled publication withdraw obsolete claims.
- Forged role advertisements cannot gain target authority; signed public queries and existing private routes remain functional.
- Test through real lifecycle/consensus/recovery seams. Run applicable release checks sequentially with full logs and true exits. Verify fresh and retained state; report actual changes and restrictions.
- Apply retained ontology policy updates only through authorized actions/atomic source editing. No ledger wipe, broad ACL bypass or automatic uncertain-write replay.

Implementation references
AGENTS.md; doc/multiwrite-architecture.md; doc/lifecycle-and-routing.md; doc/runtime-and-agents.md; archived node-instance-identity and automatic-route-recovery plans; priv/ontologies/{quod_root,quod_node,quod_signup,node_execution}.pl; src/{quod_node_actor,quod_namespace_manager,quod_directory_control,quod_directory_generation}.erl.

Review
Recommended lead: GPT-6 Astra with high reasoning for design and implementation; Fable for the independently checked architecture/security review requested by Yan. Previous Fable consultations both timed out at 180 seconds without output; there is no completed Fable approval.

"Follow-up to task_1791240698839_ywd2cg (system ontology ACLs). Yan agrees with automatic enrollment as the durable solution; manual provisioning of the current fleet alone is insufficient. No implementation has been performed for this follow-up.

Objective
Every new persistent Quod node identity automatically obtains one dedicated ordinary ontology containing its instance of the node class. Subsequent starts recover that exact identity. Define and implement consistent authority for advertising system and ordinary ontologies without making enrollment depend on root consensus membership.

Terminology and ownership
- Physical Quod runtime: loads its key, initiates enrollment and recovers its retained exact reference.
- Node identity ontology: durable node instance, active key binding, explicit ACL and ordinary hosting intentions. This is an ordinary ontology with the existing runtime, not an additional autonomous management agent/service.
- quod:node: shared node vocabulary and proposed owner of enrollment policy.
- quod:root: existing create_ontology/3 action and exact delegation to enrollment policy; system catalogue and root committee remain separately governed.
- Directory: derived leased routes; target ontology: its own ACL and membership.
Do not centralize per-node hosting configuration in root.

Observed starting point (prior deployment evidence; recheck before changing live state)
Founder has a bound node identity ontology; nine non-founder allocations lack one. Shared system ontologies are locally running. Non-founders log advertisement_author_unavailable. Creation attempted as a bare non-admitted node principal was denied.
Publisher currently partitions bootstrap/system rows from ordinary rows. System rows require a root-control author, ordinary rows a node principal. Missing authority in either nonempty partition rejects the entire publication. Merely provisioning node identities is insufficient.

Proposed enrollment
1. Reuse the restricted, key-bound enrollment pattern already present in quod:signup and root's ontology_creation_policy/2 delegation.
2. Node startup initiates the ordinary signed request once prerequisites are ready. Prolog policy derives and validates the full node founding recipe, exact requester key and identity allocation.
3. Use existing create_ontology/3, actions, atomic transactions, effect journal and lifecycle machinery. Prove how creation execution, placement on the enrolling node, self-hosting and local verified binding compose; do not assume root-side creation executes on the new node.
4. Enrollment only grants creation of the applicant's own node identity under the approved recipe. It grants neither arbitrary ontology creation nor root committee membership.
5. Retain and verify namespace, genesis anchor and node instance through the existing local pointer. Preserve one identity across process restarts and address/allocation changes.
6. Recover the original operation after uncertain outcomes or a crash between creation and binding. Never blindly reissue creation, invent replacement identity after corruption, or hide data loss.
7. Network/policy readiness uses existing notifications and recovery owners, preserving caller deadlines. No polling or second workflow engine.

Proposed advertisement policy
- A verified node identity can advertise an eligible locally ready copy.
- Shared system rows derive exact namespace/anchor authority from root's system catalogue; actor-authored system publication must not require membership in root consensus.
- Ordinary rows require exact committed hosts_ontology(NodeRef, Namespace, Anchor, discoverable).
- Private hosting rows are excluded from public generations and enumeration.
- Retain a narrow root-control bootstrap route before node identities are available, and specify publication/withdrawal when enrollment completes.
- Receiver validation verifies the active author key and appropriate committed authority for each descriptor. Reuse existing certified projections and route owner.
- Advertising does not confer target ownership, mutation access or committee membership. Target role and ACL checks remain mandatory at use.
- Amend current sender/receiver rules coherently. Do not merely suppress all system rows on non-control nodes, promote every node to root consensus, or accept arbitrary claims because a signature is valid.

Resolve in the design before implementation
- Open node enrollment versus an explicit enrollment credential/admission policy; startup automation does not by itself decide who may enroll. All limits and costs belong in Prolog.
- Uniqueness/recovery identity allocation, pending operation custody, creation executor and placement/binding sequence.
- Exact root advertisement rules after bootstrap; system membership revocation and catalogue withdrawal.
- Current discoverable hosting is the host's publication choice, not proof of target-owner publication consent. Document this boundary; stronger global confidentiality needs explicit policy.
- Root administrator invocation rights and create action prerequisites are distinct; verify actual grants instead of assuming one implies the other.
- Reconcile archived design language with current implementation and compact contracts.

Acceptance
- Real production signed paths: founder bootstrap, fresh joining node and existing fleet node without an identity enroll automatically under the selected policy.
- Restart and endpoint changes retain the same exact identity; unchanged restart performs no new creation.
- Crash before/after commit and before/after binding, duplicate request, lost response and temporary unavailability resolve the same operation without duplicate ontologies or automatic uncertain-write resubmission.
- Wrong key/anchor/instance, malformed pointer and unauthorized founding options fail closed without privilege escalation.
- Enrolled non-root-control nodes publish valid system routes and eligible ordinary routes. Invalid catalogue anchors, absent hosting facts, inactive keys and private rows are rejected/excluded.
- Removal/revocation, lease expiry and transitions between bootstrap and enrolled publication withdraw obsolete claims.
- Forged role advertisements cannot gain target authority; signed public queries and existing private routes remain functional.
- Test through real lifecycle/consensus/recovery seams. Run applicable release checks sequentially with full logs and true exits. Verify fresh and retained state; report actual changes and restrictions.
- Apply retained ontology policy updates only through authorized actions/atomic source editing. No ledger wipe, broad ACL bypass or automatic uncertain-write replay.

Implementation references
AGENTS.md; doc/multiwrite-architecture.md; doc/lifecycle-and-routing.md; doc/runtime-and-agents.md; archived node-instance-identity and automatic-route-recovery plans; priv/ontologies/{quod_root,quod_node,quod_signup,node_execution}.pl; src/{quod_node_actor,quod_namespace_manager,quod_directory_control,quod_directory_generation}.erl.

Review
Recommended lead: GPT-6 Astra with high reasoning for design and implementation; Fable for the independently checked architecture/security review requested by Yan. Previous Fable consultations both timed out at 180 seconds without output; there is no completed Fable approval.
Keep physical-door motion, pose streaming and the separate nested call-chain transcript work outside this scope."

{"title":"Expose live routes as Prolog facts beyond root and move host selection policy into Prolog","status":"to-do","priority":"medium","created":"2026-10-06","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["directory","prolog-predicates","routing","policy","quod_ask","quod_foreign_log"],"description":"# Goal

Make the live route directory fact "key K currently answers for ontology Y at address A, until lease expiry" available to Prolog policy in every hosted ontology's read-only proofs, then move host selection rules out of Erlang into Prolog and delete the Erlang ordering they replace.

Origin: Yan, 2026-10-07, during the node-enrollment routing review (frozen scope tree-02, session "Directory deployment fix review"). Separate scope from tree-02; do not fold into it.

# What exists today

- `src/predicates/quod_directory_predicates.erl` already defines `directory_host(+Ontology, ?GenesisAnchor, ?NodeKey, ?Host, ?Port)` over the ETS route index (`quod_directory:directory_hosts/1`) and `directory_control_peer(?NodeKey)` over root's committed `peer_admitted/4`. Both are registered as `query` class and are available **only while executing `quod:root`** (the `ctx_ns` check in `directory_host_5/3` and `directory_control_peer_1/3`).
- `quod_directory:directory_hosts/1` returns active public system routes only: rows with status `confirmed`, `Expiry > now`, deterministic key order; private contacts excluded. Rows carry `{Ns, system, RouteKey, NodeKey, {Host,Port}, confirmed, GenesisAnchor, Role, Expiry, Epoch, Sequence}`. The predicate currently drops `Role` and `Expiry`.
- Routes are deliberately soft state: signed, leased node-actor generations installed by `quod_directory`, rebuilt after restart, never written to consensus (module doc of `quod_directory`, `doc/lifecycle-and-routing.md` "Routes and local notifications"). Authority to advertise comes from committed facts (`hosts_ontology/4` discoverable in the node identity, `system_ontology/2` catalogue for system entries); receivers verify those before installing a route. The predicate must stay a projection of that verified index, not a second authority.
- Predicate module loading: `src/quod_app.erl` line 476 lists `[quod_directory_predicates, quod_ontology_predicates]` for root.
- Existing tests for the predicate and its live-bridge handling: `test/quod_committed_projection_tests.erl` (lines ~255, 262, 305) and `test/quod_dtx_tests.erl` (lines ~640-660, 916: sealing a plan that depended on `directory_host/5` must fail with `non_transactional_dependency`).

# Erlang selection code that would become Prolog policy

- `src/predicates/quod_ask.erl`: `open_directory_scope/1`, `choose_directory_scope/2`, `open_anchored_routes/2`, `eligible_routes/1`, `verified_plain_read_routes/3` (which confirmed validator routes an ask uses, anchor-conflict handling, local-vs-remote preference).
- `src/quod_foreign_log.erl`: `current_route_candidates/2`, `current_peer_endpoints/7`, `history_source_candidates/1`, `directory_route_hints/2` (endpoint preference order: request contact, live, certified historical, third-party supplied; capped at two per peer).
- Candidate future users: enrollment custodian choice in `priv/ontologies/quod_node.pl`, availability rules (how many confirmed hosts make an ontology available), discovery ACL (who may be told about a route).

# Hard constraints (from AGENTS.md and quod_predicates)

1. **Determinism.** A live ETS fact differs between nodes. It may be read in read-only and local proofs only. `quod_predicates` already records `live_observation` bridge use at dispatch and `quod_dtx` refuses to seal a plan that depended on one (`record_bridge_use/4`, `allowed/2`: "query reads everywhere except a deterministic policy verdict"). Keep the `query` class and the live-observation dependency marker when widening; add tests that a committed diff or atomic plan depending on the widened predicate still fails to seal.
2. **No second domain engine.** The predicate stays a read-only bridge over the directory's existing index. No copying of routes into any ontology, no new process, no cache.
3. **Replace, do not duplicate.** When a selection rule moves to Prolog, delete the Erlang ordering it replaces in the same scope and report the line delta. No parallel old/new path.
4. **Not transport.** Dissemination of routes (who pushes signed pages to whom) stays in `quod_directory_control`; this ticket does not touch it.
5. **Private contacts stay excluded** from the public fact; a private-route predicate, if ever needed, is a separate decision with its own ACL.
6. No format, wire or ledger change. No deployment authority implied.

# Proposed shape

- Widen `directory_host/5` to any hosted ontology's read-only proof context (drop the `quod:root` gate, keep `query` class). Decide whether to extend arity to expose `Role` (`validator`/`observer`) and lease `Expiry`, since host selection needs role and liveness. Suggest `directory_host/7` or a second predicate `directory_route(Ontology, Anchor, NodeKey, Host, Port, Role, ExpiresAt)`; pick one, do not keep both.
- Keep `directory_control_peer/1` root-only (it projects root membership).
- Resolve governed bridge availability before widening the context gate. Trace retained founding manifests, ordinary lifecycle/composition and compatible validator deployment; changing quod_app.erl's package module list cannot grant an existing ontology a new external-predicate capability. Do not load a bridge globally as an implicit authorization bypass. Demonstrate non-root use in a scope actually authorized to use that bridge; a demonstrated missing capability must pass the applicable architecture gate, not be hidden behind a module-file edit.
- Write the first consumer: host selection for asks in Prolog (which confirmed validator to prefer, local-first rule, anchor-conflict refusal), called from `quod_ask` through the existing predicate seam; then remove the Erlang ordering above.
- Second consumer, optional: foreign-log endpoint preference order.

# Acceptance

- `directory_host` (or its successor) proves in a read-only proof of a non-root ontology and returns exactly the active, confirmed, public rows for that namespace in deterministic order; expired and private rows absent.
- Sealing any nonempty diff or atomic plan that read the predicate fails with the existing `non_transactional_dependency` error (extend `quod_dtx_tests`).
- Ask host selection behaviour unchanged for existing CT (`quod_ask_SUITE`), with the Erlang selection code deleted and the delta reported.
- Docs: update `quod_directory_predicates` moduledoc, `doc/lifecycle-and-routing.md` "Routes and local notifications", and `doc/runtime-and-agents.md` if predicate classes are listed there.
- Standing gates (clean sequential, true exits, frozen tree) before commit; separate label bump.

# Out of scope

- Self-network-pull transport cause (documented separately in the enrollment routing evidence).
- Directory dissemination topology (fixed in tree-02).
- Making routes consensus facts: rejected, addresses churn on every reschedule and leases expire without a transaction.

## Cross-check with governed-world work
[QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) must resolve the same immutable founding-capability invariant; neither ticket approves the removed mutable-module experiment. Sharing that architectural constraint is not a reason to merge routing policy with physics or block either on an unrelated client feature. There is no backward-compatibility requirement: replace the old predicate/selection path, while preserving proofs, current identity/history and the applicable release authority. Demonstrate non-root use in a scope actually authorized to use that bridge; a demonstrated missing capability must pass the applicable architecture gate, not be hidden behind a module-file edit.

- Sealing any nonempty diff or atomic plan that read the predicate fails with the existing `non_transactional_dependency` error (extend `quod_dtx_tests`).

{"title":"Display complete current ontology state and use lenses for selection","status":"done","priority":"high","created":"2026-10-07","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["ontology","source-inspection","lens","client"],"description":"## User requirement

When an authorized user displays an ontology, show **all its content in its current state**. Keep this simple. Any narrower selection of what is seen belongs to the existing `quod:lens` ontology.

This is a separate follow-up to [QUD.7](nimbalyst://QUD.7), whose body-pose delivery, review, commit and deployment are complete. Do not reopen or expand the physics slice.

## Context and reproduction

In “Inspect objects and Prolog knowledge”, selecting `quod:node` currently shows only three `isa/2` clauses. That is neither the whole ontology nor a useful default inspection view. An earlier visit to `quod:modelling` also refused source inspection despite the system target being advertised as read-only.

The implementation conflates ontology source-read authorization with a per-predicate public API whitelist. `quod_node.pl` publishes only `public_prolog_predicate(isa/2)`; common public-source helpers enforce that list. Root advertises ordinary system-source access as read-only, but its full introspection wrappers require administrator access. The Prolog tool then has several special cases/fallbacks. The client selects the first predicate and fetches just that predicate's source.

Yan explicitly rejected this design: read permission must allow inspection of the ontology's whole current content; lenses own optional selection. This is not a request to extend the allowlist.

## Required behavior and boundaries

- Default inspection presents all current stored facts and rules for the exact selected ontology identity, including its genesis anchor. Display applied current state, including later assertions/retractions, rather than the founding file or an API subset.
- Separate source reading from execution and editing. Authorized read-only users can inspect the full ontology; this grants neither invocation nor mutation. Preserve administrator edit gates, personal-ontology ownership boundaries and unauthorized-target refusal.
- A displayed result must describe one coherent current state. Do not assemble a whole ontology from separate predicate reads at changing ledger heights. Reuse the existing owner and verified read/snapshot lifecycle; no request-time history replay, shadow knowledge base or mixed revisions. Bounded transport must leave all content reachable, with no silent truncation or hardcoded resource-budget workaround.
- Erlog system/runtime entries may optionally be omitted for clarity, using actual engine classification/provenance. Quod-authored shared, policy and domain clauses remain visible. Do not hide them by name prefix, including the stored `isa/2` rules.
- Optional filtering, grouping or selection is authored through `quod:lens`; React/Erlang render and transport the resulting view rather than inventing private selection policy. Trace existing lens selection/encoding before proposing an extension. The default remains complete without hidden pruning.
- Replace the whitelist/special-case source paths and misleading UI/docs in the same scope. Preserve legitimate signed editing, exact baselines and conflict handling. Prefer fewer concepts and production lines.
- Existing deployed ontologies retain policy in their ledgers. Package-file changes alone are insufficient: plan the authorized update through existing actions and atomic multi-ontology transactions, with outcome resolution and recovery verification. No refound or ledger wipe is authorized by this ticket.

## Implementation references

Read `AGENTS.md`, `doc/multiwrite-architecture.md` and relevant specs first. Trace `priv/ontologies/{quod_root,common_predicates,quod_node,quod_prolog,quod_prolog_eidolons,quod_gui,quod_lens}.pl`, `client/src/{prolog-edit,world}.js`, `ui/src/{PrologEditor,World}.tsx` and the existing introspection primitives. Reconcile `doc/system-ontology-acls.md`.

## Acceptance and verification

1. An ordinary authorized user inspects `quod:node` and sees its complete current stored knowledge, including domain and policy clauses beyond `isa/2`; `quod:modelling` has the same consistent read-only behavior.
2. Assert/retract through the real authorized transaction seam, refresh and verify the exact current state. Concurrent updates cannot produce a mixed-state display. Restart/recovery preserves the behavior.
3. Read-only inspection cannot edit or confer invocation rights. Unauthorized personal targets and wrong anchors remain denied; administrator editing retains baseline/conflict guarantees.
4. A lens can explicitly narrow the view through ontology-authored selection. No independent client/server allowlist silently determines visibility.
5. Exercise signed ingress and real owners using the existing lobby/source tests. Replace obsolete whitelist assertions while preserving valid authorization obligations. Verify unchanged repeat reads do not replay history, rebuild disposable state or write/sync files.
6. Record actual production-line delta and run applicable standing sequential validation gates with full logs and real child exits.

## Recommended model

**GPT-6 Astra (`gpt-6-astra`), reasoning effort `high`.** This is an engineering recommendation because the task crosses Prolog authorization, coherent owner-state reads, the existing lens model and client presentation. Keep the implementation focused and simple; stronger reasoning is not permission to invent another framework. See the [official model documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra) and [reasoning/deployment guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/deployment-checklist).","progress":100,"activity":[{"id":"activity_1791378216960_uwsb","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"action":"created","timestamp":1791378216960},{"id":"activity_1791378274557_f8oz","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"action":"updated","field":"description","oldValue":"## User requirement

"## User requirement

When an authorized user displays an ontology, show **all its content in its current state**. Keep this simple. Any narrower selection of what is seen belongs to the existing `quod:lens` ontology.

This is a separate follow-up to [QUD.7](nimbalyst://QUD.7), whose body-pose delivery, review, commit and deployment are complete. Do not reopen or expand the physics slice.

## Context and reproduction

In “Inspect objects and Prolog knowledge”, selecting `quod:node` currently shows only three `isa/2` clauses. That is neither the whole ontology nor a useful default inspection view. An earlier visit to `quod:modelling` also refused source inspection despite the system target being advertised as read-only.

The implementation conflates ontology source-read authorization with a per-predicate public API whitelist. `quod_node.pl` publishes only `public_prolog_predicate(isa/2)`; common public-source helpers enforce that list. Root advertises ordinary system-source access as read-only, but its full introspection wrappers require administrator access. The Prolog tool then has several special cases/fallbacks. The client selects the first predicate and fetches just that predicate's source.

Yan explicitly rejected this design: read permission must allow inspection of the ontology's whole current content; lenses own optional selection. This is not a request to extend the allowlist.

## Required behavior and boundaries

- Default inspection presents all current stored facts and rules for the exact selected ontology identity, including its genesis anchor. Display applied current state, including later assertions/retractions, rather than the founding file or an API subset.
- Separate source reading from execution and editing. Authorized read-only users can inspect the full ontology; this grants neither invocation nor mutation. Preserve administrator edit gates, personal-ontology ownership boundaries and unauthorized-target refusal.
- A displayed result must describe one coherent current state. Do not assemble a whole ontology from separate predicate reads at changing ledger heights. Reuse the existing owner and verified read/snapshot lifecycle; no request-time history replay, shadow knowledge base or mixed revisions. Bounded transport must leave all content reachable, with no silent truncation or hardcoded resource-budget workaround.
- Erlog system/runtime entries may optionally be omitted for clarity, using actual engine classification/provenance. Quod-authored shared, policy and domain clauses remain visible. Do not hide them by name prefix, including the stored `isa/2` rules.
- Optional filtering, grouping or selection is authored through `quod:lens`; React/Erlang render and transport the resulting view rather than inventing private selection policy. Trace existing lens selection/encoding before proposing an extension. The default remains complete without hidden pruning.
- Replace the whitelist/special-case source paths and misleading UI/docs in the same scope. Preserve legitimate signed editing, exact baselines and conflict handling. Prefer fewer concepts and production lines.
- Existing deployed ontologies retain policy in their ledgers. Package-file changes alone are insufficient: plan the authorized update through existing actions and atomic multi-ontology transactions, with outcome resolution and recovery verification. No refound or ledger wipe is authorized by this ticket.

## Implementation references

Read `AGENTS.md`, `doc/multiwrite-architecture.md` and relevant specs first. Trace `priv/ontologies/{quod_root,common_predicates,quod_node,quod_prolog,quod_prolog_eidolons,quod_gui,quod_lens}.pl`, `client/src/{prolog-edit,world}.js`, `ui/src/{PrologEditor,World}.tsx` and the existing introspection primitives. Reconcile `doc/system-ontology-acls.md`.

## Acceptance and verification

1. An ordinary authorized user inspects `quod:node` and sees its complete current stored knowledge, including domain and policy clauses beyond `isa/2`; `quod:modelling` has the same consistent read-only behavior.
2. Assert/retract through the real authorized transaction seam, refresh and verify the exact current state. Concurrent updates cannot produce a mixed-state display. Restart/recovery preserves the behavior.
3. Read-only inspection cannot edit or confer invocation rights. Unauthorized personal targets and wrong anchors remain denied; administrator editing retains baseline/conflict guarantees.
4. A lens can explicitly narrow the view through ontology-authored selection. No independent client/server allowlist silently determines visibility.
5. Exercise signed ingress and real owners using the existing lobby/source tests. Replace obsolete whitelist assertions while preserving valid authorization obligations. Verify unchanged repeat reads do not replay history, rebuild disposable state or write/sync files.
6. Record actual production-line delta and run applicable standing sequential validation gates with full logs and real child exits.

## Recommended model

**GPT-6 Astra (`gpt-6-astra`), reasoning effort `high`.** This is an engineering recommendation because the task crosses Prolog authorization, coherent owner-state reads, the existing lens model and client presentation. Keep the implementation focused and simple; stronger reasoning is not permission to invent another framework. See the [official model documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra) and [reasoning/deployment guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/deployment-checklist)."

Agreed requirements:
- Reusable GUI component classes instantiated through existing ontology semantics, usable by arbitrary components and applications, including non-lobby examples.
- Common controls in the first milestone: text inputs, buttons, selections, sliders, rotary knobs and composed forms.

- Reuse Eidolons, marks, existing client controllers, actions, reactions and agent-work owners. No parallel GUI domain engine or shadow queue.
- VR-first ergonomics, moderate adjustable panel translucency with opaque readable controls/text, accessible input alternatives and desktop operation.

- [ ] Specify the executable form/component API and trace human/agent binding and presentation through existing owners. Resolve the live-observation/material-write integration internally without reopening the settled failure behavior or hiding partial writes.
- [ ] Implement shared GUI ontology classes, composition, field/event binding and automatic authorized reaction behavior.
- [ ] Implement authenticated presentation, HUD discovery and shared question lifecycle, including concurrent openings, stale revisions, duplicate responses, cancellation, disconnects and uncertain operation outcomes.
- [ ] Extend the existing representation/controller path and deliver the common control suite with the agreed visual treatment.
- [ ] Demonstrate an elaborate form both in the lobby and on an independent application component.
- [ ] Verify behavior through production seams, including absence/refusal, event authority, agent loss, atomic question transitions and unchanged repeated-operation cost.

{"title":"Add collision-aware player movement for desktop and VR","status":"in-progress","priority":"high","created":"2026-10-07","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["physics","navigation","vr","client"],"description":"## Goal and current state
Deliver collision-aware player movement for desktop and VR, movement before expanding the interaction repertoire. Existing retained simulation, signed pose/control and checkpoint foundations have been implemented/committed; [QUD.8](nimbalyst://QUD.8) is done, not a future prerequisite. They do not establish movement acceptance in Yan's normal lobby or on a physical headset.

[QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) owns the missing generic optional-physics integration and real signed normal-lobby desktop collision acceptance. This ticket remains in progress until its movement and physical Vive/WebXR acceptance below is demonstrated. Existing hardware startup/preflight or a separate physics view is not that acceptance.

## Scope and acceptance
- Define and verify explicit agent/body and camera local position/orientation; distinguish observer travel, commanded body travel and tracked head motion. Use existing Prolog policy, physics authority and signed controls, not a client collision authority or second engine.
- Desktop commanded movement cannot cross declared solid floors, walls or obstacles; movement alongside them remains usable.
- Physical Vive/WebXR: validate landing, teleport destination/path behavior for supported modes, contact feedback, tracked-head handling, correction and comfort on intended hardware. Record actual landing/contact/tracking/comfort evidence, not desktop or synthetic XR substitutes.
- Test occupied spawn/reposition/teleport, moving doors and idle-body contact, rotated/non-box supported geometry, collider edits/deletion, stale physical revisions, disabled/nonphysical/denied/unavailable states, revocation, reconnect and authority changes.
- Reuse explicit ontology collision definitions. GLBs, Eidolon/picking bounds and rendered shape are not collision authority. Local responsiveness must preserve authoritative controls and truthful correction/disconnect states.
- Live collider changes propagate by existing committed-diff subscriptions, not new synchronization or manual re-adoption. No backward-compatibility branches; no automatic observer fallback.
- Measure unchanged repeated-operation cost and real update invalidation through production owners; preserve original-operation resolution for uncertain writes.
- Keep the actual current lobby's identity/history and established openings/roof/console. October 9 identity evidence is historical after the separately authorized October 10 refound; establish a fresh signed personal-lobby baseline.

## Ownership of related work
[QUD.3](nimbalyst://QUD.3) is the physics umbrella; [QUD.27](nimbalyst://QUD.27) supplies normal-world integration, [QUD.36](nimbalyst://QUD.36) the deferred durable door blocked/closed interaction, [QUD.9](nimbalyst://QUD.9) held objects, and [QUD.25](nimbalyst://QUD.25) the general GUI. Do not reopen completed hot-control/source-inspection foundations or infer that their commits pass this ticket.

Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md, doc/multiwrite-architecture.md and existing movement evidence/plan before work. Do not reopen completed hot-control/source-inspection foundations or infer that their commits pass this ticket.

Enable optional governed physics in existing ontology worlds and ordinary signed client views. The first acceptance target is Yan's actual current personal lobby, preserving its exact identity and history. This is a generic capability, not a lobby special case, and remains a prerequisite of [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26).

- Prolog decides whether a world is physical and whether simulation is enabled. [QUD.33](nimbalyst://QUD.33) supplies space and physical_space semantics; class membership alone does not load native predicates, allocate resources or authorize control. Ontology and space are independent classes. Text/3D ontology representation work in [QUD.32](nimbalyst://QUD.32)–[QUD.35](nimbalyst://QUD.35) is not a prerequisite for the entire physics slice.
- There is no backward-compatibility requirement: replace superseded paths, remove old/new branches and do not introduce a separate physics ontology merely to accommodate old code. Preserving this lobby's identity/history is a distinct requirement; no automatic refound, data wipe or history rewrite.
- Domain policy, actions, authorization and resource budgets stay in Prolog; external Erlang predicates are governed interfaces. One physics authority and one mutable owner for each truth; no second domain engine, private knowledge base or hidden fallback.

## Architecture gate
Read AGENTS.md, doc/world.md, doc/multiwrite-architecture.md and existing ontology lifecycle/action/recovery owners. Trace existing composition and ordinary founding/bridge deployment before selecting the smallest missing capability. A linked normally founded physics scope is a candidate, not an accepted default; any boundary must be justified by governance/lifecycle, not backward compatibility. Do not silently resurrect the removed external_predicate_selection/reconcile_modules experiment.

Specify exact world/instance/body/agent references, capability authorization, compatible participating validators, concurrent-proof conflicts, rollback, recovery and withdrawal. Validator compatibility for the chosen deployment is not permission for permanent backward-compatibility code. Neither changing a package file nor declaring a class changes a retained founding manifest. If the selected design needs a new capability-evolution contract, bring that concrete gap to the applicable architecture/deployment gate rather than bypassing immutable provenance.

## Existing subscriptions, not another propagation path
A live collider defined in ontology A and consumed by subscribed physics authority P follows A's committed diffs through the existing subscription/verified-projection owners. An authorized edit must update the effective collider automatically; no manual re-adoption per edit, mirrored mutable collider store, polling loop, new diff broker or second synchronization protocol. Deliberately pinned reusable shape recipes are different from live referenced instances and must be explicit, never the default imposed to solve linkage.

Trace quod_runtime subscription handling and quod_foreign_log retained projections through the current local physics resource selector. Demonstrate any missing dependency-to-install wiring, extend that existing owner, and preserve subscribe-before-snapshot, exact source/body/structure revision fencing and installation notices. Recovery restores current verified state; correctness cannot depend on replaying or receiving every best-effort reaction. Related durable changes/receiver consequences form one existing atomic transaction; no post-commit repair workflow to reconnect artificially split writes.

## Physical definitions and normal views
- Author explicit physical geometry, agent/body binding and camera local position/orientation in Prolog. Support the native adapter's supported shapes through shared validation, not only a hardcoded box. Visual GLBs, picking bounds and Eidolon geometry are not collision authority. Preserve real openings, roof and console geometry.
- Future noncubic voxel/chunk geometry uses the same explicit geometry, resource-policy and revision contract; missing collision coverage is unknown, not empty. Terrain streaming is not part of this slice.
- Reuse the existing signed projection/control protocol in the ordinary view. Track visible-world, acting-agent, physics and actual authorization/geometry dependencies, including a disabled selection that later becomes enabled; current source/simulation-only subscriptions are not automatically sufficient.
- Preserve anchored instance/body identity, decorative marks, authored parents/attachment frames and camera transforms under one pose writer. Discovering physics only from a lobby rule is insufficient if the current lookup is in the acting agent's ontology.
- Distinguish observer travel, commanded body travel and tracked head movement. Unavailable physics must not silently switch a controlled body into observer travel.
- Distinguish nonphysical, disabled, denied, recovering and unavailable. Handle occupied spawn/reposition/teleport, collider edits/deletion, moving doors, revocation, reconnect and authority changes. Commit, installed state and mechanically fulfilled placement are separate; durable occupancy conclusions use existing authenticated observations, not live-query proof exemptions.
- Admission/withdrawal and any exclusive body assignment use the designated owners and existing atomic transitions. Resolve uncertain operations by original identity, never new submission. No generic inter-simulation handoff is assumed.

## Evidence and acceptance
October 9 signed lobby evidence and the removed experiment are historical: doc/evidence/player-movement/live-lobby-20261009/README.md and cleanup-20261009/README.md. A separately authorized October 10 refound is recorded under doc/evidence/hot-controls/deployment-256-refound/. Therefore establish the fresh signed personal-lobby identity/history baseline before acceptance; neither the old anchor nor the system lobby-vocabulary anchor identifies it automatically.

1. Generic production-owner tests across at least two world identities, including a non-lobby and a nonphysical case. Cover concurrent admission/edit/withdrawal, authorization, rollback, recovery and stale fences.
2. A real committed remote collider change reaches the subscribed installed physics owner through the existing path. Measure exact affected invalidation and unchanged repeat work: no history replay, projection/native geometry rebuild or storage write/sync caused by unchanged checks. Distinguish legitimate simulation stepping and real durable updates. Preserve current conservative world fencing/per-predicate OCC; do not claim row-level precision.
3. Real signed desktop collision acceptance in the normal view of the same existing lobby, preserving identity/history, console and openings. A fixture/simulated test world is not a substitute.
4. Physical Vive/WebXR landing, contact, tracking and comfort remain required separately by [QUD.26](nimbalyst://QUD.26). Durable real-lobby blocked/closed door acceptance is [QUD.36](nimbalyst://QUD.36); do not confuse moving-door collision coverage with that consequence acceptance.
5. Coordinate a single server writer and existing release authority. Client testing does not authorize broader runtime mutation or deployment.

{"title":"Document Quod terminology for ontologies, instances, spaces and representations","status":"to-do","priority":"medium","created":"2026-10-10","authorIdentity":{"email":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com","displayName":"yan.guiborat","gitName":"Yan Guiborat","gitEmail":"yan.guiborat@gmail.com"},"createdByAgent":true,"tags":["architecture","ontology","documentation"],"description":"## Goal
Create a concise, source-checked terminology reference for this plan. Explain existing words rather than introducing another ontology taxonomy.

## Scope
- Define ontology (authoritative Prolog code/state, ACL and history boundary, also an instance of the ontology class), class, instance, space, physical space, agent, lens, encoding, Eidolon, mark, anchored reference, route/contact, body and physics authority.
- Distinguish subclass from instance membership; code/state ownership from spatial containment; ontology contents from a presentation of them; marks from body identity; source/interface inspection from permission to invoke or edit.
- Record Yan's choice: ontology and space are independent classes. Every accessible ontology may have 3D/text/policy representations; representation does not entail space membership. A space may be nonphysical; physical_space is a subtype of space. Physics enablement remains governed Prolog policy.
- Do not introduce “subject” as a new user-facing domain category. Existing source terms such as subject(Target, Entity) may be explained as current API syntax, not another kind of object.

Make each exact ontology available as an ordinary instance of the ontology class, reusing class/instance selection, lenses, encodings, Eidolons and marks. This refines the existing model, not a second ontology-object system.

## Scope
- Derive identity from existing namespace/genesis-anchor and lifecycle owners; expose authorized current source, explicitly declared interfaces, contacts/routes and ACLs through their real owners. A contact address is a route, not identity or a copied mutable directory field.
- Replace the ontology-specific selection/dispatch fork with the ordinary applicable-Eidolon path. Preserve exact target anchors through class diagrams, text/policy panels and 3D marks; a mark occurrence is not a new ontology. Do not assume every Eidolon is a code workspace.
- Preserve existing private ontology discovery boundaries; root's system catalogue is not a global list of personal ontologies.
- Expose ACL rules under the target's read policy, distinguishing source read, policy read, invocation, content edit and policy edit. Where effective permissions are displayed, make them bounded, context-relative advisory results; actual actions reauthorize against current state. Do not execute mutations as permission probes, invent a privileged arbitrary-goal oracle, or treat *_query/1 helpers as a universal public API catalogue.
- Location and state ownership remain independent under ACLs. Ontology and space are independent classes (Yan's explicit choice): a 3D representation does not imply isa(ontology, space), transfer ownership or enable physics.

## Acceptance
System and owned non-system ontologies use the same representation selection, with correct read-only/editable/denied behavior. Wrong anchors, private targets, stale permissions and unauthorized policy edits fail at the real owner. Authorized edits use existing transactions and exact-outcome handling. Multiple views stay on the same committed contents/history; unchanged inspection does no replay/rebuild/write/sync. Remove superseded ontology special dispatch, not retain an old/new compatibility path.
